business_problem: System Research needed employees to find information buried in internal documents and rulebooks without depending on supervisors or colleagues for search keywords and document-location hints.
solution_summary: System Research built an internal knowledge-search assistant around IBM Watson Discovery and IBM watsonx.ai to help employees find material buried in internal documents and rulebooks. Watson Discovery indexes the company's internal content and returns relevant results inside a chat-style interface, while watsonx.ai generates answers that match the intent of the user's question. During a three-week UI pilot, the team displayed Discovery results at the bottom of the chat field and tuned the experience to improve answer quality and make search more natural. The design keeps source retrieval connected to generated responses so staff can move from question to document evidence without asking supervisors for keywords or hints, turning a fragmented, non-cross-searchable repository into a more usable internal search workflow.

solution_components.name: IBM Watson Discovery
solution_components.role: Searches internal documents and rulebooks and surfaces supporting results inside the chat experience.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Generates answers that match the intent of employee questions using the retrieved enterprise content.

data_flow: Employees ask questions in natural language; Watson Discovery searches internal documents and rulebooks, the chat UI shows retrieved results beneath the conversation, and watsonx.ai turns that retrieved context into answers aligned with the user's intent.
business_outcome: System Research reduced the time needed to get information by making enterprise search natural-language driven, faster, and easier for employees to use on their own.
